Paper: Zhang & Wu (2022), N-rGO for trace antibiotics
Issue class: Concentration/volume basis ambiguity and fitted-capacity extrapolation
Specific unresolved issue: The original PDF says each test used 80 mL antibiotic solution plus 20 mL N-rGO dispersion (0.5 mg/L), giving 0.01 mg N-rGO. Fig. 2a caption states C0=10 μg/L; Table 1 reports qe(exp)=80.58–90.21 mg/g. If C0 applies to the 80 mL feed before dispersion addition, the maximum is 80 mg/g; if it refers to the final 100 mL mixture, the maximum is 100 mg/g. Reported values therefore exceed only the former interpretation, and the paper does not make the concentration basis clear. Table 2 q_m values are fitted Langmuir parameters (about 562–1266 mg/g), not measured uptake; Fig. 2b shows the experimental isotherm data at trace concentrations.
Why it matters: The trace-level graphene-derived result is important, but the exact concentration basis determines whether the largest measured q_e values fit the experimental mass balance. Fitted q_m values greatly exceed observed loadings and should not be mistaken for demonstrated capacity.
Next action: Keep as source-reported; seek clarification of whether C0 is before or after addition of the 20 mL sorbent dispersion and exactly how dose is defined. Do not call the q_e values impossible or normalize them.
Manuscript treatment until resolved: Retain condition-labelled qe only with concentration-basis caveat; exclude fitted q_m from cross-paper capacity rankings. Explicitly classify N-rGO as graphene-derived, not biochar.
Status: Open — ambiguity confirmed, no proven violation
